new_test_original: D chapter 1 only; chapter 2+ private withheld
training_originals: B first two fully paragraph-annotated; chapters 3-4 preliminary
genre_transfer: high-fantasy original -> frontier science-fantasy ecology, renamed and functionally analogous sites/actors
observations: A frontier planet has a long forested ridge with distinct neighboring summits and independently active small wildlife.
At a depression mid-way along one peak, a slight young gatherer carries a wicker salvage basket of botanical supplies.
Young gatherer studies a frequently reread old guild manual describing exceptional practitioners.
Young gatherer longs to become an exceptional practitioner but believes lacking a rare innate interface makes it impossible, expecting ordinary healer work instead.
Despite slight physique, youth is a practiced and agile vertical climber.
Moist wind and looming storm clouds advance independently of all character intentions.
A respected older mentor predicted a valuable rain-dependent secretion at a particular high-altitude overhang.
The youth chooses to ascend with a rope and small container after observing the predicted storm.
Near the ridge summit a perforated overhang has many cavities and a difficult underside ledge.
Ordinary walking cannot reach the underside; without flight, a prepared offset rope swing can cross the gap.
Youth offsets the tether, grips rock face, and waits at risk of falling as wind and rain become violent.
Fierce storm blows branches and small animals off the ridge; they have independent vulnerability.
Heavy rainfall causes dark liquid to seep out of the under-ledge rock and flow downward.
The mechanism producing the liquid is not known to the youth.
Fluid changes color after a delay, creating a narrow collection window.
Youth waits for color change, then swings to collect a limited container volume while briefly stationary near the overhang.
Several large autonomous nest-guarding arthropods emerge from cavities and charge toward the gatherer.
Youth releases one rope to evade attack; this creates immediate lethal fall risk rather than guaranteed safety.
A small sentient companion arrives on a separate rope and catches the falling youth.
Youth and companion descend to a lower ledge; youth prioritizes protecting the collected vial.
Companion privately carries an unidentified dark shard and initially hides it when questioned.
Nest guardians autonomously continue pursuing down the rock face.
Companion appears anxious when pursued, but displayed fear may not reveal genuine motive.
Youth states pursuing creatures do not cross the lower ridge boundary, based on past escapes.
Youth promises the companion part of the collected fluid; companion visibly cheers up.
Both travelers know repeated installed rope routes on the ridge; navigational shortcuts offset slower running speed.
Guardians seem unwilling to cross some rock zones, taking detours despite being faster; reason not identified.
Guardians stop at foot of ridge and independently retreat to their nests.
Storm dissipates after the escape; it is not ended by the youth.
At forest fringe, distant settlement lights mark home, separate from cliff and nest.
Companion already consumes a negotiated portion of the scarce fluid but wants more.
Companion has a prior friendship with the youth that began with conflict several years earlier.
Companion independently offers unidentified shard in exchange for more liquid.
Youth gives another portion while saying the shard is worthless; economic transaction and social generosity coexist.
Companion drinks, becomes euphoric, drops both remaining vial and shard, and leaves independently.
Youth ends the episode holding reduced fluid and unfamiliar shard, without knowing shard origins or properties.
Nothing in observed episode proves the shard is magical, that the fluid has unlimited supply, or that the nest guardians follow a moral law.
Future training success, future power gains and future use of the shard are not yet observed.
questions: Recover, in prose not just observation IDs, causal constraints for storm, geomorphology, extraction, predation, escape and finite goods; classify witnessed fact, belief and unknown.
Explain how a smaller companion and nest guardians maintain independent motives and behaviors not controlled by protagonist.
If P0 refuses the trip, which processes continue and which events no longer follow automatically?
If companion values shard more than resource, does original exchange remain compulsory? Preserve freedom and relational history.
Do not guess exact future magic rules, promotions or cliff accidents from what was not observed.

calibration.principle: A character's wish about an object's healing properties is belief, not observed effectiveness.
Material progress consumes finite recovery assets; a benefit can cost someone else.
Institutional eligibility and actual admission are different; discretion and exceptions do not erase default policy.
Individual knowledge follows actual observation and communications; narrator knowledge does not teleport.
Repeatable environmental effects do not prove complete hidden mechanisms.
Off-screen institutions and rival groups persist independently of protagonist activity.
Named small spaces, directed routes, availability and access must survive world relocation; geography is not decoration.
Minor worker agency and side-payment/response/promise must be kept separate; future fulfillment is uncertain.

budget_warning: Treatment receives additional calibration tokens; any gain is confounded by extra context. No independent adjudication guaranteed.
